svg.text: Motorized Pool-Cover Winch: Wiring Diagram (24 V DC, battery powered)
All power at the pool is extra-low-voltage DC from a battery. No mains wiring at the starting block. Charge away from the water.
IP67 BATTERY / CONTROLLER BOX (yellow box in the CAD). Every cable leaves through an IP68 gland.
while the safety loop is made
IP67 roller lever at the fairlead
without a dot are not connected.
1. The key S1, both E-stops (box S2, pendant S4) and fuse F2 form one series loop that powers K1's coil. Open any of them
and K1 drops out: the motor and the controller lose power at the same moment.
2. Hold-to-run: the motor turns only while IN or OUT is held. The firmware ramps up over 0.5 s and stops on release.
3. Overload: above 18 A for 0.3 s (about the 500 lbf rated pull) it stops and beeps, so it can't rip the block loose.
4. S3 is wired normally closed, so a broken wire reads as 'limit reached' and winding in is blocked (fails safe).
Crimp a stopper ball on the rope about 1 m before the tarp's tow bar.
5. Below 22.0 V the controller won't start. Recharge with a 29.2 V LiFePO4 charger, key OFF.
6. Mount F1 within 18 cm of battery +. D1 goes across the K1 coil; C1 sits right at the driver's power input.
7. 24 V DC is not a shock hazard, but keep the box out of splash zones. Never bring mains power to the block.
